newsitem.title: USA: South America cotton imports to be record -- ICAC.
newsitem.headline: South America cotton imports to be record -- ICAC.

text.p: South American countries will import an estimated 600,000 tonnes of cotton in 1996/97, a record for the region and 11 percent of world trade, the International Cotton Advisory Council said Monday.

"The rise in South American imports represents a significant shift in the structure of world cotton trade," the ICAC said in a monthly report, which also said a smaller share of cotton was going to Europe and East Asia.
One-fourth of U.S. exports and nearly all of Argentina's cotton exports go to the Western Hemisphere. The record for South American imports was 540,000 tonnes in 1993/94.
ICAC said Brazil might import 490,000 tonnes in 1996/97, Colombia 40,000 tonnes, and Chile and Peru 30,000 tonnes each.

World cotton output was pegged at 19.2 million tonnes in 1996/97 and 1997/98, ICAC said. Chinese output "may fall below four million tonnes" in 1997/98. U.S. output was estimated at four million tonnes.

"Cotton area in India may decline in 1997/98," ICAC said. "Higher yields in Pakistan, following a difficult season in 1996/97, may lead to increased production. Better weather and an early start to planting is expected to boost production in Central Asia."
